title: Mamdani, NYC officials give update on ICE shooting

segments.transcript: Good evening, everyone. Around 4 p.m.
This afternoon, a New Yorker was shot by ICE agents in Marble Hill.
Many of the facts surrounding this shooting are still unclear.
ICE agents surrounded the man's vehicle before opening fire.
They wore construction vests and masks that concealed their faces.
There was no reasonable way to identify them as ICE agents.
School had just gotten out.
The street was crowded with families and children.
When ICE agents opened fire, a five-year-old child, a five-year-old child, was in the backseat of the car.
Thank God that child is physically unharmed.
For the past two hours, I have been on the phone with President Trump and Secretary Mullen,
Negotiating the release of the man ICE agents shot.
Those negotiations were unsuccessful. Just moments ago,
ICE put the man in an unmarked vehicle and whisked him away. Let me say this plainly.
What happened today was an outrage.
Tonight, a five-year-old child sits traumatized and terrified.
Tonight, millions of our neighbors are wondering whether they will be safe on our streets, in our schools, at their work sites.
Tonight, New Yorkers across the five boroughs are asking whether their civil liberties will be respected, whether law and order is supposed to look like a man carrying a long gun wearing a mask.
We know that ICE is rotten to its core.
Today's shooting is only further devastating confirmation of what we have long known, which is that ICE operates with impunity,
That they sow chaos and terror across our country, that they have killed far more of our neighbors than they could ever have claimed to save.
I also want to say something on a personal note.
I stand here not just as the mayor of our city, but as someone who is proud to be an immigrant in our city.
And I know that these kinds of raids, this kind of terrorizing of this city, leaves the 3 million immigrants of this city asking if they are safe here,
If they belong here, if this too can be their home here.
We will not normalize ICE's viciousness.
We will not accept its cruelty.
We know, and I have said this directly,
Whether to the President or to the public,
ICE undermines public safety.
It makes us less safe.
New York City will not stand by while ICE agents shoot New Yorkers.
And we will not back down from the demand that so many, including myself, have put forward time and again.
This is an agency that must be abolished. Thank you.
With that, I am now going to turn it over to our police commissioner, Jessica Tisch. Thank you, sir.
I'm here to brief you on an incident that occurred earlier today involving ICE agents in the Marble Hill right behind me.
The information I'm about to provide is preliminary and it is subject to change.
At 4.04 p.m., the NYPD received two 911 calls reporting a person's shot and shots fired in the vicinity of 2 Marble Hill Avenue.
At the same time, a federal agent called 911 requesting the fire department and then asked for the NYPD.
According to our preliminary investigation,
Federal immigration agents were conducting a targeted enforcement operation in an effort to take an individual into immigration custody.
At the time that individual was inside a gray Honda CRV with a five-year-old boy whom we believe to be his son.
NYPD Argus Camera captured the victim backing into a parking spot in front of a fire hydrant right behind me.
At that time, one plainclothes federal law enforcement officer approaches the driver's side window with his gun drawn.
Another plainclothes officer also approaches the vehicle by the driver's side headlight.
The vehicle then starts to move forward and goes out of camera view.
The Argus cameras do not capture the discharge.
Based on evidence Since collected the scene, we know that at least one ICE agent discharged seven rounds,
Striking the driver in the neck below his left ear.
Members of the NYPD's 50th Precinct Conditions Team were responding to an unrelated call nearby when they heard the report of the shots fired,
And they responded to that scene.
When they arrived, they encountered several men in various forms of attire, including including some in construction-style vests,
Face masks, and at least one carrying a long gun.
Our officers also encountered the injured individual handcuffed and seated on the ground.
Our officers immediately placed him into an NYPD vehicle and rendered aid.
They transported him to New York Presbyterian Allen Hospital, where he arrived in stable condition.
Our officers' actions were captured on body worn camera. I want to be clear,
The NYPD had no involvement in the federal operation prior to the shooting and no members of the NYPD were on scene at the time of the shooting.
Additional NYPD officers arrived and secured the scene for the purpose of preserving evidence.
At least seven shell casings were covered at the scene along with the victim's vehicle which had ballistic damage to the front windshield.
The back window of the car was also shattered.
That vehicle was positioned perpendicular to the road.
An ICE vehicle, which is a gray four-door sedan, had damaged the left front panel and the lower panel fully disconnected.
With respect to the child who was inside the vehicle.
Pursuant to a wellness check, the NYPD located the child safe and in the care of a family member.
The individual who was shot has been identified as 28-year-old Oscar Belgol.
He has two prior arrests in New York City, one for robbery in 2023, in which he pleaded guilty to fourth-degree grand larceny and received five years probation,
And one for criminal sale of a controlled substance in 2025, which is still pending.
At this time, federal agents have exercised their authority to take over the investigation.
I will now turn it over to our attorney general.
There is no explanation for these tactics.
There is no explanation for federal officers firing this many rounds into a car that has a five year old in the car.
There is no explanation.
We are standing here so close to the site of where this actually took place.
And look at how many people live right here this is a residential neighborhood we are right here by a subway and the pretext of ice is in their words to keep this country safe how is it keeping
Anyone safe to have as you just heard from the police commissioner individuals wearing construction vests in masks with long guns residents have no idea if these are law enforcement
Agents or if they are simply attacking someone on the street and when it comes to ice it begs the question what's the difference there There is no explanation for this.
I made clear to the president, to the secretary, our request that ICE agents leave the scene entirely as well as the demand that ICE stop its enforcement
Actions in New York City.
These actions are making the city less safe.
They are making New Yorkers terrified.
You are hearing from New Yorkers right now, anguish, pain,

Anger at the fact that here in this city, the world city, that immigrants have to wake up every morning and not know if they can live the lives that they should be able to live and help to build this city.
I'm proud to stand here alongside our public advocate, our attorney general, assembly members, city council members, state senators,
Elected officials at all level, united in the belief that there is no justification for what we have seen today.
And we know that what we have seen today is but a microcosm of what ICE does on a daily basis across this country.
How can that be how we describe public safety? It can't be.
And I've shared that with the president. I've shared that with the secretary.
This city wants ice out.
We want ice out of our city, ice out of our schools, ice out of our hospitals, ice out of our streets, ice away from our kids.
We want that because we want to keep the city safe.
We do not need them to do so.
All they do is terrorize the city.
